# 1 Enoch Chapter 22 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 22 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 22:1 — "hollow places" vs. "hollows" vs. "chambers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hollow-places" (hyphenated) | Literal rendering of Ge'ez compound |
| LOGOS | "hollow places" | Standard English two-word phrase |
| PNEUMA | "hollows" / "chambers" | First "hollows" then shifts to "chambers" for theological clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "hollow places" throughout. EMET's hyphenation is unnecessary; PNEUMA's shift from "hollows" to "chambers" introduces inconsistency. "Hollow places" preserves the spatial imagery of carved-out recesses without over-interpreting as "rooms."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:4 — the spirit of the dead man

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the spirit of a dead man, and his voice went forth to heaven and made supplication" | Literal, paratactic |
| LOGOS | Same structure | Converges |
| PNEUMA | "the spirit of a dead man. His voice was crying out toward heaven in urgent appeal" | "Urgent appeal" adds emotional weight |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET. "Made supplication" is precise theological vocabulary for petitionary prayer to God; PNEUMA's "urgent appeal" is interpretive. The paratactic structure reflects the Ge'ez syntax.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 22:6 — Abel's ongoing suit

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men" | Literal; "suit" for legal petition |
| LOGOS | "he makes his suit against him until his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth and his seed is annihilated from among the seed of men" | Formal; same structure |
| PNEUMA | "He is crying out against Cain until the last of Cain's descendants is wiped from the face of the earth and his line is cut off from the human race entirely" | Names Cain; paraphrases "seed" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Suit" preserves the forensic legal register appropriate for Abel's petition. PNEUMA naming Cain explicitly adds a clarity not in the text at this point (he was named in v. 7 of the prior sentence). "Seed" for the Ge'ez term is the standard rendering and should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:10 — the eternal imprisonment

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "great pain till the great day of judgment, and punishment, and torment of those who curse for ever, and retribution for their spirits. There he shall bind them for ever." | Literal; archaic "for ever" |
| LOGOS | "great pain until the great day of judgment, and of punishment and torment of those who curse forever, and retribution for their spirits. There he shall bind them forever." | Formal; normalizes "forever" |
| PNEUMA | "great torment here until the great day of judgment — the day of punishment and everlasting condemnation. On that day they will receive full recompense, and they will be bound there forever." | Paraphrase; shifts structure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The difficult Ge'ez syntax of "punishment and torment of those who curse forever" is best handled formally; PNEUMA's paraphrase alters the structure too freely. EMET's "for ever" (two words) is an archaic spelling; normalized to "forever."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:12 — sinners who will not be raised

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their spirits shall not be slain in the day of judgment nor shall they be raised from thence" | "Slain" for judgment-destruction; "thence" archaic |
| LOGOS | "their spirits shall not be slain on the day of judgment, nor shall they be raised from there" | Same verb; modernizes "thence" |
| PNEUMA | "They will not be judged on the final day, nor will they be raised to life — they simply remain there" | "Not be judged" softens; "raised to life" expands |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Slain" preserves the unusual Ge'ez verb that suggests the fourth group is neither condemned (slain in judgment) nor resurrected — a distinct category from the others. PNEUMA's "not be judged" loses this nuance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
